fix: redirect-written files use LF line endings (GNU parity) (#1)

PowerShell's console layer terminates every output line with CRLF, so
executor-captured stdout written via > / >> carried \r\n — making byte
counts and file contents diverge from coreutils (seen across the Ark
model matrix: 'head -2 f > out.txt; wc -c out.txt' reported 13 where GNU
gives 11 for an 11-byte LF stream). Normalize CRLF→LF on captured
stdout/stderr before result assembly and file writes.

Found via the Volcano Ark multi-model benchmark (kimi-k2-thinking,
deepseek-v4-pro both tripped over it); verified with two new integration
tests asserting LF-only redirect output and GNU byte counts.

Co-authored-by: 20000419 <20000419@users.noreply.github.com>

feat: nudge models to batch commands per call in tool description (#2)

Benchmark data (docs/benchmark-deepseek-v4-pro.md addendum): the wall-time
gap of fauxnix vs bundled one-shot shells scales with call granularity —
models issuing 2-3 tiny calls per task paid ~30% overhead, while bundled
callers matched native speed. One sentence in the tool description flips
the default toward bash-idiomatic 'a && b; c' batching.

Co-authored-by: 20000419 <20000419@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: resolve redirects against cwd after each segment

runPlans captured the entry directory once, so
`cd src && echo data > out.txt` wrote out.txt in the old
directory while two separate session calls wrote it under src.

Re-read session.cwd after every completed segment and pass
that same directory to the next child process. Open redirects
in parsed source order, keep those descriptors open, and
write the full captured buffer (retry short writes) so
`rm out.txt > out.txt` cannot recreate the path.

fix: keep intentional CRLF from exact writers (#12)

Blind `\r\n` → `\n` rewrites broke `printf 'a\r\nb' > out`
(Codex P2 on #1). Only normalize when every LF is part of a
CRLF pair and the buffer ends with a newline — the shape of
PowerShell Write-Output — so fx-write/printf payloads stay
byte-exact.

fix: promote the next word when command-position [@] is empty

Bash removes an empty ${X[@]} in command position so the following
word becomes the command. Only keep a synthesized empty command when
a prefix/suffix affix remains.

feat: add command -v and command NAME passthrough

Agents look up tools with command -v. Map builtins to /usr/bin/NAME
(same as type/which) and resolve other names on PATH. Bare
`command NAME args` runs NAME without aliases (fauxnix has none).

feat: source/. reads NAME=VALUE assignment files

Agents commonly `source .env`. Accept comment lines, optional export
prefix, and matching quotes. Other syntax still fails loudly — no
functions or arbitrary shell.

feat: read / read -r assigns piped lines to session vars

Agents parse tool output with `cmd | read -r VAR`. Store the first
stdin line (or IFS-split fields) via the same Env/SETVALS path as
export so a later segment sees the value.

fix: refuse set -e/-u/-x instead of silently ignoring them

A silent no-op makes `set -e` look like errexit is on. Fail with
exit 2 so agents see the lie. `set` / `set --` stay no-ops.

feat: expand ${#name} string length and ${#name[@]} count

${#name} is the scalar string length; ${#name[@]} is the array
element count. Length expansions are not argv splats.

feat: accept backtick command substitution as $(...)

Models still emit `cmd`. Parse backticks into the same CmdSub node
so they share the quoted/unquoted newline contract.

feat: translate if/then/else/fi as a compound command

Parse the whole if as one command so it stays in a single PowerShell
process. elif is rejected until a follow-up; if in a pipeline errors.

feat: translate for name in words; do ...; done

Parse the loop as one compound command so the body shares a
PowerShell process. The loop variable is written through SETVALS.

fix: empty command-position [@] is a null command; promote via handlers

A vanished ${X[@]} with no words left is exit 0, not command-not-found.
Remaining words are translated at compile time so printf/true keep
their handlers. Nonempty splat path wraps argv as [object[]] to
survive PS 5.1 single-element unwrap.

GNU find's ! and -o were in the path-end stop set but never compiled, so find . ! -name '*.ts' -delete deleted the named set. fix: response budgets must not corrupt redirected files; truncate at UTF-8 boundaries (Codex-review P1s)

Both verified broken on published v0.9.0:
- stdoutLimit/stderrLimit were passed to the host frame for file-redirected
  segments too, so 'printf AAAAAAAAAA > f' with stdoutLimit 4 wrote 4 bytes
  to the FILE; defaults (8MiB/1MiB) silently clip larger redirected files.
  File-redirected segments now run uncapped (limit 0); the returned-data
  budget is still enforced by the existing final clipUtf8.
- byte-level truncation could split a multi-byte codepoint; Node's decoder
  then rejected the buffer and fell back to GBK — '你好世界…' under a 7-byte
  budget came back as mojibake '浣犲'. The cut now backs off to a valid
  UTF-8 sequence boundary (lead-byte scan, max 3 bytes).

Regression tests for both; repro outputs in the PR.

release: v0.9.1 — P1 hotfix (redirect budgets + UTF-8 boundary)

fix: per-stage redirect ownership and >/dev/null discard

Stop concatenating every pipeline command's redirects onto the whole segment. Prep still walks all redirects left-to-right; captured stdout/stderr follow the last stage; FAUXNIX_STDIN_FILE follows the first stage only.

A non-first < file replaces the pipe as that stage's stdin (printf x | cat < fruits.txt | head -1 reads the file). Last-stage >/dev/null discards captured stdout instead of printing it. RFC: docs/rfc-redirect-fd-ownership.md (#131).

fix: native argv via fx-native instead of PS 5.1 splat

PowerShell 5.1 `& name @array` drops empty arguments and eats embedded
quotes, so node/git see a different argv than CreateProcess. Route
literal and dynamic native invocations through fx-winargv (CRT quoting)
and System.Diagnostics.Process. Stdio uses ReadToEndAsync — a scriptblock
on Task.Factory.StartNew cannot run on the thread pool in PS 5.1.

Names that are not Applications (splat expanding to echo) still fall
back to the call operator. xargs remains a follow-up. RFC:
docs/rfc-native-argv-fidelity.md (#131).

fix: last-wins >/dev/null against a later stdout redirect

A later `>file` after `>/dev/null` left devNull set, so apply discarded
stdout and wrote an empty file. Clear the other of {devNull, stdoutFile}
on each stdout redirect. 2>/dev/null no longer undoes a prior stdout
discard. Prep recognizes cwd\NUL as the DOS device after path.resolve.

docs: sync command-specs.md with the live CommandSpec registry

#144 spec'd remaining file commands but left docs/command-specs.md and the
README CommandSpec list on the old cp/mv/rm/touch/tee/grep/head/du set.
Regenerate the markdown from specsMarkdown(), update README, and lock the
doc to the generator with a unit test.

Refs #143.

fix: GNU head --bytes=-N / --lines=-N print all but last N

GNU head --bytes=-N prints all but the last N bytes. The bytes path used
Min(-N, length) then clamped to 0, so negative counts silently emitted
nothing. Use max(0, length + count), matching the lines path.

-0 and N >= size still yield empty. Tests cover the translation formula
and --lines=-1 / --bytes=-1 / positive counts on a known file.

Relates to #143.

fix: print FAILED when powershell.exe spawn fails

runCheck() only listened for stdout and close. Missing powershell.exe emits an unhandled EventEmitter error and never printed FAILED. Copy the ps-host spawn error listener: print FAILED with the message and exit 1.

fix: grep -e/--regexp repeats OR-accumulate patterns

parseWords keeps only the last -e/--regexp value, so grep -e a -e c matched only c. Collect every short and long regexp and match if ANY pattern hits; -v inverts the combined result once.

fix: re-split printf-style stdin lines in grep and text-filters

Non-terminal printf emits one object with embedded newlines. STDIN_LINES now re-splits via fx-splitlines like text-io STDIN_INLINES, so `printf 'a\nb\n' | grep b` matches. Single-line pipes (echo hi | grep hi) stay identity.

fix: treat hard links as regular files, not symlinks

GNU hard links are regular files. Inspectors treated any truthy Get-Item.LinkType (including HardLink) as a symlink. Use one predicate: SymbolicLink or Junction (junctions stay links on Windows).

fix: fx-native empty argv, cmd shims, and pipe readers

PS 5.1 unwraps an empty object array to null, which became a phantom empty argument. Null-check before wrapping. cmd/bat cannot be CreateProcess targets with UseShellExecute=false; launch them via cmd.exe /d /s /c. Start ReadToEndAsync before writing stdin so a chatty child cannot fill the 64KB pipe.

and eats embedded quotes. Call fx-native instead (stdout as pipeline
strings, fx_exit already set). Curl/wget keep fx-netguard before launch.
System32 tar.exe preference is unchanged. gzip/zip stay translated.

fix: xargs native invoke via fx-native instead of PS 5.1 splat

xargs still built `& $fx_cmd @fx_argv`, which drops empty argv on PS 5.1.
Invoke through fx-native with a typed object array (no splat). fx-native
already records $script:fx_exit from ExitCode.

Default xargs splits stdin on blanks; -I stays line-oriented.
-t / -n / --no-run-if-empty and builtin-reject unchanged.

feat: CommandSpec for text-io leftovers (echo/printf/cat/tail/wc)

Spec echo -n/-e/-E (and bundles), printf with no option flags, cat -n/-b/-s/-E/-T/-A, tail -n/--lines -c/--bytes -q/-v with -f/-F unsupported, and wc -l/-w/-c/-m. Unknown options fail loud. find/xargs/nl/tac stay unspec'd.

printf --help is a usage error; format operands that look like flags (printf '%s' -n) still compile because echo/printf stop option scanning at the first operand.

Relates to #143.

fix: emit grep -F -o matches in input order

Collect -F -o hits by position and length so multiple -e needles emit left-to-right (GNU leftmost-longest) instead of per-pattern.

fix: quote cmd metacharacters when launching .cmd/.bat

cmd.exe /c treats &, |, and () as operators. CRT quoting left --flag=a&b raw, so the /c tail could split and run trailing text.

Wrap the /c command in extra quotes (/s strips that pair) and CRT-quote args that contain & | ( ) < > ^. Existing ./hit.cmd still runs; dump-args.cmd keeps a&b as one argument.

fix: last-wins per fd so 2>&1 >/dev/null keeps stderr

Captured output was merged then wiped by a sticky devNull flag, so cmd 2>&1 >/dev/null dropped diagnostics. Apply each stream to its left-to-right fd destination (caller / file / NUL) instead.

echo hi >/dev/null stays empty. cat missing 2>&1 >/dev/null returns the diagnostic on caller stdout. >/dev/null 2>&1 still discards both.

fix: accept ls --color as an implemented no-op

Agents emit --color=auto constantly; after CommandSpec it was a usage
error. GNU ls already strips color on a pipe unless always. Consume
--color=WHEN without emitting ANSI.

fix: hint python3 and .sh on Windows command-not-found

fx-native 127 was just `bash: python3: command not found` with no hint.
Mac-trained agents emit python3; Windows has python/py. Do not alias
python3->python (wrong interpreter): hint + 127 only.

When Get-Command Application and Get-Command both miss:
- python3 / python3.exe: try python or py on Windows
- names ending in .sh: existing errors.ts hint (fx-native never emits
  the PS "is not recognized" line that used to carry it)

Also fail loud on xargs -0 (was silently ignored) and point find -exec
at find ... -delete / grep -r instead of xargs rm (hits XARGS_BUILTIN_MSG).
